6	## 2026-08-29 — Native plan-and-self-review step for hard-task design rounds, not superpowers:writing-plans
7	Context: asked to have planner-architect use the `superpowers:brainstorming`/`writing-plans`
8	skills for complex tasks (write a plan, self-review it, hand it to the engine).
9	Decision: build the same rigor (numbered plan, self-review for coverage/placeholders/
10	consistency/scope/ambiguity) directly into `design-round`'s procedure instead of invoking those
11	skills. Two reasons: (1) `superpowers:brainstorming` hard-gates on human approval before any
12	implementation step — incompatible with an unattended pipeline run; (2) both skills are
13	machine-local plugins, not committed to this repo, so referencing them would silently no-op on
14	every cloud routine run (the pipeline's primary execution mode).
15	Consequences: the plan-and-self-review discipline now runs identically local or cloud, with no
16	external dependency. If those skills are ever made repo-portable and their approval gate made
17	optional for headless use, this can be revisited.
18	
19	## 2026-09-06 — Model policy: cheap implementer, heavy planner and reviewer
20	Context: the owner wants token spend cut without losing quality. Previously `classify` sent
21	hard tasks to an opus or fable *engine*; sonnet/haiku only implemented easier tiers. Reviewer
22	and QA models were fixed by frontmatter/profile, so the `deep`/`max` profile could silently put
23	browser-qa on opus.
24	Decision: split the pick in two. `engineModel` is haiku (trivial) or sonnet (everything else,
25	hard included) — never opus/fable. `planModel` is opus (explicit spec) or fable (thin spec) and
26	drives the design round, the replan, and code-reviewer. Every design round now produces a
27	full implementation plan (previously hard-only), explicit enough that sonnet executes it
28	rather than reasoning it out. test-qa-engine and browser-qa are always sonnet; the CTO gate
29	is pinned to opus in the workflow (never fable). The orchestrator passes every model
30	explicitly. Revisits 2026-08-29: `superpowers:writing-plans` may be used for the plan when it
31	is present in the skill listing (local runs); the native a–c step remains the cloud fallback.
32	`superpowers:brainstorming` stays excluded — its human-approval gate is still incompatible
33	with unattended runs.
34	Consequences: opus/fable spend moves from implementation (the longest stage) to two short
35	stages (plan, review). Plan quality is now load-bearing for hard tasks — a thin plan will
36	show up as sonnet build failures and verify fix-cycles, which is the signal to fix the plan,
37	not to raise the engine model.

224:## Rule AUTH-9: Sensitive endpoints are throttled per view, and the cache backend is what makes that real
225-
226-`backend/backend/throttles.py` defines `UserRateThrottle` subclasses (account-keyed when authenticated,
227-IP-keyed otherwise), applied per view with `@throttle_classes`; rates live in
228-`REST_FRAMEWORK["DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES"]`. Auth-relevant scopes: `auth-login` 30/h (`login_view`,
229-`google_login`), `auth-signup` 10/h (`signup_view`), `auth-refresh` 60/h (`SessionRefreshView`),
230-`score-submit` 60/h (`log_session`), `user-search` 120/h (`search_users`, `search_friends`),
231-`friend-action` 60/h (`send_friend_request`, `block_user`). There is deliberately no
232-`DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES`. Exceptions by design: `logout_view` and `profile_photo_view` are unthrottled.

## 2026-09-29 — Show the country of your online opponent: standard vs hard, sonnet vs opus
Context: fullstack P1 card, one-line spec, no override. Users have no country anywhere (`backend/users`
has no country/geo field or header read; every `country` hit in the repo is NBA player data). The relay's
`publicUser` (`multiplayer_server/src/index.js`) sends only id/username/photo/rank/points to opponents, and
`PlayerCard`/`OnlineMatch` render that. Shipping it needs a country source the spec does not pick: a
user-set profile field (`CustomUser` column + migration + `user_payload`/`update_profile`, all AUTH-11) or
geo-IP at identify time (a request header on the relay handshake or Django; a privacy call), then a new
field in the relay's opponent payload, then a flag/label in the VS intro and results. `standard` was
defensible (each piece follows an existing pattern — `profile_photo` already rides the same path), and
sonnet was defensible (09-23 precedent: AUTH-9/11 surfaces handled by `risk: high` review, not an engine
upgrade).
Decision: `difficulty: hard` (multi-area, changes the multiplayer opponent payload, likely a migration on
the shared dev/prod DB), `risk: high` (AUTH-11 `users/models.py`/`user_payload`/`update_profile` or the
relay `identify` handler, plus new data exposed to strangers), `needsDesignRound: true`, `engineModel:
opus` provisional — the 2026-09-29 "risk: high → opus" override postdates the 09-23 sonnet precedent and
wins; the design round may finalize simpler steps (the `PlayerCard` flag, the payload field) as `[sonnet]`.
`planModel: fable` — the country source, its privacy/opt-out rule, and how it is displayed must be invented.
Consequences: the design round must pick the country source first (profile field vs geo-IP) and state what
a stranger in random 1v1 learns; if geo-IP is chosen, check whether the relay's host gives a country header
for free, and never add a paid geolocation service (money rule). The backend commit ships before the relay
and frontend ones, and the relay must tolerate old clients/users with no country.
"
